Introduces decision = "prompt-user" in managed requirements.toml prefix rules, forcing a human decision independent of automatic review, hook allowances, and saved approvals. The clearest policy-control addition in the batch.

  5. #58119 — Add experimental Guardian review for injected thread commands. Exposes thread/guardianReview to assess an idle thread's final injected exec_command without executing it, returning the call ID plus assessment (or null when exec policy skips approval).

  6. #58075 — Use serving assessments for adaptive Guardian review. Matches final serving assessments to responses/output items and reuses them instead of asynchronous scoring, so low-risk actions can be fast-pathed.

  7. #58040 — Preserve native tool-call evidence through Guardian review. Retains original function-call metadata even when the call has aged out of live history — required to review encrypted multi-agent messages correctly.

  8. #58122 — Add an incremental exec tools feature flag. Registers incremental_exec_tools as an under-development, default-off feature exposed in the config schema — the scaffolding for incremental tool exposure.

  9. #58091 — Update default models for memory extraction and consolidation. Switches to gpt-6-luna for extraction and gpt-6.1-terra for consolidation when the provider doesn't mandate a backend-specific ID — i.e., cheaper/smaller models for memory maintenance.

  10. #58129 — Persist subagent relationships before creating child storage. Prevents orphaned child history that parent-subtree deletion can't discover; a relationship-write failure now rejects the spawn.

Also notable: #58144 (new codex.additional_context count/byte/truncation metrics), #58121 (centralized provider request auth checks with retry on credential change), #58134 (model-migration guidance prefers documented replacements), #58110 (scoped RUSTSEC-2026-0418 ignore for Windows-only libz-sys).

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #30332 — Background updates for Codex CLI without blocking startup. Proposes a Claude Code–style flow: check/download in the background, prompt to restart when ready, instead of forcing an update decision at launch. Startup friction is a recurring complaint across CLI tools.
  • #57967 — 1–2 free Codex usage resets per month for ChatGPT Plus. Asks for the currently promotional resets to become a predictable monthly allowance; framed as retention/plan-value rather than an entitlement demand.

Q&A

  • #8582 — Search/Find in the active chat history (4 👍). Ctrl-F always targets the code editor regardless of focus; no search context menu exists in the Codex canvas. Basic navigability gap that grows with conversation length.
  • #5210 — Any way to clear the text area? No discovered shortcut for clearing the prompt input after an accidental large paste — small UX papercut, long-lived thread.

Show and tell

  • #57746 — Zozo: an inspectable issue-to-PR example and a review checklist for coding-agent work. Ships a public issue/diff/CI trace plus a checklist for vetting agent output. Useful pattern for teams that need auditable agent runs.
  • #57591 — toli — let Codex and Claude Code collaborate, even on different machines. Apache-2.0 tool for direct agent-to-agent communication across developers' machines, motivated by divergent local context during pair debugging.
  • #58093 — OpenFusion: orchestrator and router for subtask handling. Routes each subtask to the cheapest capable model with a judge step that escalates on poor results — cost-optimization around Codex/agent workloads.
  • #58104 — Kilobat: networking for AI agents (and humans). macOS menu-bar network monitor that tracks Codex, Claude Code and Gemini traffic, with an open-source CLI + MCP so agents can inspect network state themselves.
  • #56337 — Off the Wall: recall your past corrections before Codex answers. MIT-licensed, keeps corrections in the user's own words and quotes them back to Codex or Claude Code — a lightweight persistent-preference layer.
  • #58031 — Using Codex with current Alibaba Cloud documentation and official citations. Reports that generated cloud config is plausible but needs verification against live endpoints/regions/models — an argument for grounded doc retrieval in domain-specific work.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Configurability of agent behavior. The top-upvoted issue (#34455, 22 👍) wants configurable request_user_input timeouts; #34070 wants CODEX_HOME/CODEX_DIR respected; #58127 (PR) makes tooltips honor a preference. Theme: stop hardcoding policy and UI defaults.
  • Desktop/CLI parity and consistent state. Env-var handling, cloud-environment discovery (#58145: CLI picker returns HTTP 200 [] while desktop shows a published env), and archived-chat deletion (#43197) all point at divergent code paths between surfaces.
  • Platform parity, especially Windows. Computer Use (#54532, #57371), sandbox execution (#55230), policy denial messaging (#56722), /approve discoverability (#57350), file/PDF access (#58139) — the largest single cluster in the window.
  • Transparent, actionable safety and policy errors. #58138 and #58141 (both 10-29) report cybersecurity guardrails blocking ordinary C/C++ and local Git integration work; #56722 asks for the blocking rule and a recovery path instead of "blocked by policy."
  • Credential and secret management as a first-class capability (#58148) — driven by usage shifting into infra/deploy/production work.
  • Browser and extension integration robustness — Chrome Web Store availability (#36319), IAB session binding (#57107), unsupported extension sidebars (#58133).
  • IDE ergonomics — in-chat search (#8582), clear-input shortcut (#5210), respecting the default editor for file links (#47702).
  • Cost/usage flexibility — predictable usage resets (#57967) and community-built routing to cheaper models (#58093).
  • Non-blocking update flows for CLI (#30332).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows is the weakest surface. Command execution inside the app sandbox fails outright (HRESULT 0x80070020, #55230); authorized commands are rejected as "blocked by policy" with no rule identified and no recovery action (#56722); /approve is undocumented-in-UI and returns "no command found" (#57350). Multiple independent reports converge on the same experience: the permission system says no, and won't say why.
  • Safety guardrails produce false positives on ordinary work. Two reports in a single day (#58138 C/C++; #58141 local Git integration) describe repeated interruptions of plainly authorized development tasks by cybersecurity filters — a direct productivity tax that also undermines trust in the approval flow.
  • Silent state and cache bugs. IAB drops the tab's session binding before an action (#57107); PDF refresh keeps stale content because the cache key omits conversationId (#56862); archived-chat deletion no-ops (#43197). Silent failures are costly in agent workflows because the agent, not the human, is the one observing them.
  • Regressions land on the stable desktop channel. Worktree icons vanish in 26.1023.50603 (#57620); the VS Code extension freezes the whole IDE on Linux/Wayland in 26.1021.22027 (#57759, fixed only by downgrading). Users are effectively debugging release gating.
  • Configuration is not honored consistently. The desktop app ignores CODEX_DIR/CODEX_HOME (#34070) and, per #58145, disagrees with the CLI about which cloud environments exist — forcing users to duplicate or manually sync setup.
  • Extension distribution is unreliable. A months-old Chrome Web Store outage (#36319) blocks the documented install path, and unsupported extension sidebars (#58133, OKX Wallet) narrow what the built-in browser can host.
  • Locale-specific breakage. Incomplete zh-CN localization (#27255) and zh-CN-only Computer Use failures (#54532) suggest locale handling is under-tested outside en-US.
  • Long-conversation navigability and input control remain unaddressed. No in-chat search (#8582) and no clear-input shortcut (#5210) are small requests with outsized daily cost, and both threads are months old.

Prepared as an analyst digest. Alpha release notes were empty in the source data; PR intent is inferred from titles and descriptions.

Gemini CLI — google-gemini/gemini-cli

Gemini CLI Community Digest — 2026-10-30

Today's Highlights

No new releases shipped in the last 24 hours, but community activity remained heavy: 46 issues and 37 PRs were updated, with the bulk of attention still on agent/subagent reliability. Two P1 agent bugs — misleading MAX_TURNS success reporting (#22323) and the generalist agent hanging indefinitely (#21409) — continue to draw the most discussion and reactions. On the PR side, contributors pushed a broad set of hardening fixes around checkpoint/restore correctness, shell-substitution security, retry deduplication, and CI test coverage.

Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

Hot Issues

  1. #22323 — Subagent MAX_TURNS reported as GOAL success (P1) A codebase_investigator subagent reports status: "success" and Termination Reason: "GOAL" despite its own output saying it hit the turn limit before performing analysis. This is a correctness/trust problem for any automation that branches on agent status. 13 comments and 2 👍 make it the most-discussed issue of the window.

  2. #21409 — Generalist agent hangs forever (P1) Simple operations like folder creation hang indefinitely once the CLI defers to the generalist agent; users report waiting up to an hour. The workaround — instructing the model not to use subagents — is telling, and with 8 👍 it's the highest-reacted issue in this batch.

  3. #19873 — Zero-dependency OS sandboxing + post-execution intent routing (P2, effort/large) Proposes leaning into Gemini 3's native bash affinity by letting models chain POSIX tools (grep, sed, awk) inside an OS-level sandbox, then routing on post-execution intent. This is the architectural counterpoint to the safety concerns raised elsewhere. 9 comments, 1 👍.

  4. #21968 — Gemini under-uses skills and subagents Anecdotal but widely resonant: the model won't invoke custom skills (gradle, git) or subagents unless explicitly told, even when highly relevant. Directly undermines the value of the extensibility surface. 7 comments.

  5. #22745 — EPIC: assess AST-aware reads, search, and codebase mapping (P2) Parent epic investigating whether AST-aware tooling reduces misaligned reads, cuts turns, and trims token noise. Related investigations (#22746, #22747) are tracking tilth/glyph/ast-grep as candidates. 7 comments.

  6. #24246 — 400 error when >128 tools are available (P2) The CLI surfaces a 400 once the enabled tool count crosses the threshold, with no graceful scoping. A hard scalability ceiling for users with many MCP servers or extensions. 3 comments.

  7. #22672 — Agent should stop/discourage destructive behavior (P2) The model reaches for git reset or --force when safer alternatives exist, and lacks guardrails around destructive DB/resource operations. Security-adjacent and likely to shape policy work. 3 comments, 1 👍.

  8. #21983 — Browser subagent fails on Wayland (P1) The browser subagent terminates with Termination Reason: GOAL on Wayland sessions, i.e., a failure masked as success — the same reporting pattern as #22323. Linux/Wayland users are effectively blocked from browser automation. 4 comments.

  9. #22267 — Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (P2) AgentRegistry merges settings correctly at init, but the Browser Agent bypasses them entirely — including maxTurns. Config drift of this kind is especially confusing when combined with the hang/turn-limit issues above. 4 comments.

  10. #23571 — Model litters workspace with temp scripts (P2) When restricted to shell execution, the model generates edit scripts across arbitrary directories, creating cleanup overhead before any clean commit. A concrete workflow tax on shell-only configurations. 3 comments.

Also worth watching: #20079 (symlinked agent files not recognized), #22598 (surface subagent trajectories via /chat share), #22741 (background local agents via Ctrl+B, 2 👍).

Key PR Progress

  1. #30034 — Honor .git/info/exclude and core.excludesFile in shadow repo Fixes a data-loss class of bug where /restore reverted or deleted files that should have been ignored under Git config rules. Important for anyone using checkpointing with local-only excludes.

  2. #30035 — Prevent $-pattern corruption in LLM prompt templates (P2) Migrates summarizer.ts, llm-edit-fixer.ts, and sessionSummaryService.ts from String.replace(placeholder, value) to a single-pass safeTemplateReplace(), eliminating dynamic-value interpretation bugs in prompt construction.

  3. #30031 — Gate background log stream init on execution lifecycle (P2) Addresses a model-config edge case when gemini-2.5-flash is explicitly selected alongside useLatestFlash and dynamic model configuration. Prevents premature log-stream initialization.

  4. #30023 — Run SDK tests in PR CI, fix AgentLoopContext mock (P2) Re-enables 6 skipped GeminiCliSession.sendStream() tests and adds the SDK package to the others CI shard. Meaningful reduction in untested surface area.

  5. #29918 — Report working/blocked/idle status via OSC 7501 The TUI now emits terminal program-status reports so multiplexer tabs can show which session needs attention. A quality-of-life win for multi-session workflows (size/xl).

  6. #30020 — Drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry On mid-stream retries, both the failed and successful attempts' ToolCallRequest events were being executed — meaning side-effecting commands could run twice. High-value correctness fix for the agent loop.

  7. #30029 — Make command-substitution blocking user-configurable (P3, help wanted) Adds security.allowCommandSubstitution (default false) to replace the hardcoded block on $(), backticks, and process substitution in the shell tool. Fixes #27393; trades convenience against a deliberate safety default.

  8. #30026 — Treat project temp paths as local in untrusted-flag checks Stops the CLI from prompting for confirmation on its own helper scripts under ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/..., a recurring friction point after shell output leaks script paths into context.

  9. #30019 — Preserve session history during tool output masking Prevents the first user prompt from being dropped when resuming sessions whose tool outputs were masked, by not writing the API-shaped getHistory() view back into storage.

  10. #29977 — Honor cancellation in read_background_output (P2, help wanted) The tool previously ignored its abort signal and would sleep out the full delay_ms before reading anyway. Complements #29978, which fixes dropped boundary/oversized lines in the same tool.

Also merged/closed this window: #30012 (429 cool-down countdown in the loading indicator), #30006 (PowerShell CIM fallback for Windows IDE process lookup), #29989 (\n escape corruption across core/cli), #30024 (undici 7.10.0 → 7.30.1).

Feature Request Trends

  • Agent orchestration maturity. The largest cluster by far: backgroundable local agents (#22741), shared memory / parallel subagent collaboration (#18287), delegating build-fix loops to the generalist (#22602), and a dedicated subagent eval strategy (#22601). Subagents are clearly the strategic center of gravity.
  • Observability and debuggability. Requests for subagent trajectories in /chat share (#22598), subagent context in /bug reports (#21763), and better agent "self-awareness" of its own flags and hotkeys (#21432) all point to the same gap: users can't see what the agent is doing.
  • Token-efficient, structure-aware code intelligence. The AST epic (#22745) plus #22746/#22747, "Tactful Extraction" (#19561), and persistent file-based task tracking (#18836) form a coherent push to reduce context bloat and context rot.
  • Safety with escape hatches. Sandboxed native bash (#19873), discouraging destructive git/DB commands (#22672), and configurable command substitution (#30029) suggest the community wants secure defaults plus explicit opt-outs.
  • Browser agent resilience. Session takeover/lock recovery (#22232) and respecting settings.json (#22267) are recurring asks from anyone running persistent browser sessions.
  • Policy granularity. Per-workspace policy autoaddition (#18397) reflects demand for repo-scoped rather than global trust decisions.

Developer Pain Points

  • Silent hangs and masked failures. The two dominant P1s — the generalist agent hanging (#21409) and MAX_TURNS being reported as GOAL success (#22323, and the same pattern in #21983) — are the most damaging class of bug because they defeat scripting, CI, and user trust simultaneously.
  • Configuration that isn't honored. The Browser Agent ignoring settings.json (#22267) and symlinked agent files being silently skipped (#20079) both produce "I configured it correctly and nothing happened" experiences with no diagnostic signal.
  • Scale ceilings on tooling. The 400 error past the tool threshold (#24246) punishes exactly the power users who invest in MCP servers and extensions.
  • Workspace hygiene. Temp scripts scattered across directories (#23571) and /restore touching ignored files (#30034) both turn a clean commit into manual cleanup.
  • Platform-specific breakage. Wayland browser failures (#21983) and Windows path/process issues (#30033, #30006) recur; Windows fs.stat returning dev: 0 on Node 22.12–22.16/23.x caused every secure file read to fail before #30033.
  • Correctness bugs in the agent loop itself. Double execution of tool calls on retry (#30020), \n escape corruption (#29989), and $-pattern mangling in prompt templates (#30035) are low-level but high-blast-radius — they silently alter behavior rather than failing loudly.
  • Evaluation infrastructure is not yet trustworthy. #23166 ("evals bleed") and #23313 (a steering eval had to be commented out) show the team itself is still stabilizing the measurement layer, which slows confidence in agent-quality claims.
GitHub Copilot CLI — github/copilot-cli

GitHub Copilot CLI — Community Digest

Date: 2026-10-30 · Source: github.com/github/copilot-cli

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but 38 issues were updated, with activity concentrated on authentication/platform bugs and ACP (Agent Client Protocol) parity gaps. The long-running org-entitlement failure #552 remains the most-discussed thread at 31 comments, while several high-severity resource-consumption reports (#5254, #4613) continue to draw attention. Fresh triage items include a broken copilot --cloud provisioning path and a /copy Markdown→HTML regression.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #552 — Failed to list models: 403 unauthorized (OPEN, 31 comments, 👍4) The highest-traffic thread in the repo. Users in orgs with Copilot CLI enabled still cannot enumerate models, blocking basic usage. The comment volume (spanning from Nov 2025 to now) signals an unresolved entitlement/mapping problem on GitHub's side rather than a simple client bug.

  2. #2165 — Ubuntu keychain support is broken (OPEN, 5 comments, 👍22) Highest-reaction item in this batch. Two distinct defects: incorrect docs for the keychain workaround, and secret-tool-related auth failures. Linux users consider this a first-class platform-support gap.

  3. #4802 — PRU quota wiped out, likely tied to Assisted Permissions (OPEN, 8 comments) Billing-impacting report from a Pro annual/legacy request-based user. Community reaction is cautious but concerned — quota accounting regressions erode trust quickly, especially with no clear remediation path.

  4. #4851 — Azure MCP server fails sending HTTP request (CLOSED, 6 comments, 👍10) Rust runtime BrokenPipe when validating an Azure API Center MCP registry — a "broke overnight" enterprise regression that was closed, suggesting a fix landed. Notable for the 10 upvotes and enterprise MCP reliance.

  5. #4275 — ACP: expose contextTier as a session config option (OPEN, 7 comments, 👍4) The interactive /model picker supports mid-session context-tier changes; ACP clients can only set it at spawn. A clear parity request from a GitKraken integrator — evidence that third-party ACP consumers are now a real constituency.

  6. #2109 — ACP: support ask_user / ask_question extension method (OPEN, 4 comments, 👍8) Only session/request_permission is exposed today, so custom ACP clients can't surface clarifying questions with structured answers. Well-received (👍8) and architecturally significant for the ACP ecosystem.

  7. #5254 — 1.0.103: main process grows to 37 GiB during long parallel-agent session (OPEN, 2 comments) 37.3 GiB physical footprint after ~6h19m on a 32 GiB Mac, with 133M malloc allocations and 10.7 GiB fragmentation. This is the most alarming stability report in the batch — long-running resumed sessions with parallel sub-agents are effectively unusable.

  8. #4613 — 1.0.80+ regression: MCP schemas eagerly injected, +354K startup tokens (CLOSED, 3 comments) The CLI apparently stopped deferring MCP tool schemas, injecting the full ambient catalog into the first request even for trivial prompts. A direct cost/latency regression for anyone with a large MCP setup; closed implies triage action.

  9. #4576 — includeCoAuthoredBy: false not inherited by task subagents (OPEN, 2 comments, 👍5) Subagents still add the Co-authored-by: Copilot trailer, contradicting an explicit settings.json opt-out. Small surface area, real compliance annoyance for teams with strict commit-attribution policies.

  10. #5275 — Support default-deny tool permissions with explicit allowlist in non-interactive mode (OPEN, 1 comment) --deny-tool always overrides --allow-tool, and some tools are allowed by default, so CI pipelines cannot enforce a strict allowlist. A foundational request for anyone running the CLI unattended.

4. Key PR Progress

No pull requests were updated in the last 24 hours.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this period.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • ACP parity with the interactive TUI is the clearest emerging theme: contextTier as a session option (#4275), ask_user extension methods (#2109), correct session/prompt semantics that don't kill background sub-agents (#4555), and OAuth refresh-token use instead of browser prompts (#5229). Integrators want ACP to be a first-class surface, not a subset.
  • Deterministic, policy-driven non-interactive mode: strict tool allowlists (#5275) and settings inheritance into subagents (#4576). Headless CI use is outgrowing the current permission model.
  • Configuration discoverability: publishing a JSON schema for providers.json (#5287) and adding the documented but missing --fusion-tier flag (#5290). Users are reverse-engineering BYOK and model-tier settings.
  • Cross-platform identity integration: Linux secret storage (#2165), macOS XARA keychain partitioning (#4273), Windows Entra broker token cache (#5236), and GHE-aware proxy/token forwarding for gh in sandbox mode (#5286).
  • MCP lifecycle maturity: correct Enterprise/Entra scope handling (#5061), Datadog OAuth token exchange (#5058), and lazy schema loading to control startup token cost (#4613).
  • Context-window ergonomics: reliable rollover/checkpointing (#5205) and compaction thresholds that don't fire at 50% on high-effort models (#4571).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Authentication and platform integration remain the weakest area. Keychain/secret-store issues span Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows in this single window, plus Enterprise/data-residency login confusion (*.ghe.com mislabeled as Enterprise Cloud, #5280). Enterprise users hit this first and hardest.
  • Resource and cost blowups in long sessions. A 37 GiB process footprint (#5254), a runaway copilot-file-search thread pinning CPU while idle (#4710), and 354K tokens of eager MCP schema injection (#4613) all point at insufficient bounds on background work and startup payload.
  • Silent or premature failures in non-interactive/ACP mode. session/prompt unconditionally aborting the session (#4555), plugin custom agents activating in --prompt but not interactively (#4592), and copilot --cloud failing instantly with an opaque internal server error (#5289).
  • Billing/quota opacity. The PRU wipeout report (#4802) is low-volume but high-severity; quota changes tied to feature toggles need clearer accounting and rollback guidance.
  • Regression churn between minor versions. /copy now returning HTML instead of Markdown (#5288), an October theme change reducing heatmap/highlight readability (#5056), and compaction behavior shifting in 1.0.80 (#4571) suggest a fast release cadence outpacing regression coverage. Version numbers cited in this window range from 0.0.355 to 1.0.105.
  • Long-tail issues without closure. #552 has been open since November 2025 with 31 comments and no resolution — a visible signal that org-level entitlement bugs fall into a black hole, which discourages further high-quality reporting.
OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-10-30

1. Today's Highlights

Two releases landed within 24 hours: v2.2.2 enables image generation by default for providers that expose image models, and v2.2.1 adds /goal for goal-driven sessions that keep running until a reviewer confirms completion. The tracker is dominated by free-tier/quota confusion (the megathread has 104 comments) and reports of v2.2.1 sessions hanging at "Working". Meanwhile, maintainers are landing a wave of core work: a tree-sitter-free shell permission scanner, Code Mode schedule checks, and by-reference media blobs in the TUI.

2. Releases

  • v2.2.2 — Image Generation by Default: when a connected provider supports image models, agents can call experimental_image_generate with no extra configuration. Preferred model is configurable via experimental.image_generate.model (#60258).
  • v2.2.1 — Keep Working Toward a Goal: /goal <objective> in TUI/Desktop keeps the session running until a reviewer confirms the objective is met; /goal pause|resume|clear control the loop (#59437).
  • process-daemon v0.3.3 — opencode-pty 0.3.3 (protocol 7) from packages/process-daemon, published to npm as @opencode/pty@0.3.3.

Release PR: #60337 release: v2.2.2 brings versions and changelog back to dev.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #59387 Free tier issues: read this first — 104 comments, 9 👍. The canonical funnel for free-tier failures: "Free usage exceeded", resets that never happen, and Desktop version mismatch. Highest-engagement thread in the repo and the clearest signal that quota messaging needs work.
  2. #33356 Unbounded growth of the event table (13GB+ opencode.db) — 45 comments, 12 👍. Long-lived instances balloon to ~13 GB because message.updated.1 snapshots are never pruned or compacted, filling volumes to 97–99%. Top-voted issue; a real operational risk for headless deployments.
  3. #58786 Desktop sessions hang in Working/Thinking after Oct 22 Bun runtime update — Reproduces in brand-new sessions, no error surfaced. Points at the runtime migration rather than session corruption.
  4. #60330 v2.2.1 stalls at "Working" all day in OpenCode GO — Fresh report on the current release; 15-minute latency on a trivial "Test" message while the Console build works. Suggests a regression worth bisecting against v2.2.2.
  5. #56288 external_directory ask is skipped for shell — reproduced, severity: high. File tools enforce the rule, shell does not; a path outside the workspace can be written silently. Directly relevant to the tree-sitter removal work in PR #60332.
  6. #46371 Hidden LLM calls billed but absent from session cost — Title generation and summaries call LLM.stream() but never persist token usage; billing-level evidence revives an auto-closed report. Cost transparency is a recurring trust issue.
  7. #57012 Allow insecure HTTP for authenticated remote MCP servers on internal networks — v2.0 strictly enforces TLS for authenticated MCPs; internal-network users are blocked. PR #60039 (per-server TLS trust) is the upstream response.
  8. #60320 Active Go subscriber hard-blocked by rate limit on Beam Free — Paid account, but beam advertised as unlimited returns an inescapable rate-limit error. Pairs with #60317 on the retry-countdown that never resolves.
  9. #7487 exec variable substitution — 8 comments, 5 👍, open since January. Long-running request to reuse config variables inside exec; a small config-ergonomics gap that keeps resurfacing.
  10. #46378 Unicode × (U+00D7) triggers HTTP 400 on GLM-5.3-Flash — Deterministic gateway [1210] API parameter invalid on standard characters. A narrow but fully reproducible provider-compatibility bug.

Also worth tracking: #46035 MCP children accumulate until OOM (closed), #46164 /compact lacks a context-fit check, and #60328 free usage exceeded with zero usage.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #60332 refactor(core): finish moving shell permission checks off tree-sitter — Shell permission checks now run on the built-in scanner across all channels, dropping 2.3 MB of embedded tree-sitter WASM and fixing eight shell-parsing edge cases. Directly addresses the class of bypasses in #56288/#46398.
  2. #60140 feat(core): Code Mode checks with static tool scanning for schedules — Schedules can run a JavaScript if/until check before waking a session, with no model call and no allowlist to maintain. Behind experimental.*. Builds on merged #60137.
  3. #60028 feat(core): let a Code Mode check decide when a schedule fires — Closed precursor to #60140: if: { type: "code", code, allow } evaluates state, now, and runs and returns { wake, state, message? }.
  4. #60116 feat(tui): load stored images by reference, like desktop — TUI requests stored images by reference and downloads only on display, matching Desktop. Active only with experimental.media_blob; a meaningful step for large-image sessions.
  5. #60102 fix(core): keep permission reasons and feedback in MCP tool failures — Denials previously collapsed to Unable to execute <server>_<tool>, hiding the rule and user feedback from the model. Better self-correction after a deny.
  6. #60120 fix(core): send execute progress at most every 100 ms — Nested execute calls previously emitted 2N ever-growing snapshots; throttling cuts bandwidth and UI churn on large programs.
  7. #60039 feat(mcp): per-server TLS trust for remote MCP servers — Adds a tls config block (ca_file, …) per remote server; explicit trust first, trust-on-first-use to follow. The supported answer to #57012.
  8. #60315 feat(core): integration.connect and integration.use policies — MDM-enforceable org policies for Console workspaces; supersedes OPENCODE_CONSOLE_REQUIRE_ORG (#58159). Enterprise deployment is becoming a first-class concern.
  9. #60084 fix(core): require one-way V1 upgrade acknowledgment — One-time confirmation before startup imports V1 history, clarifying that adopting V2 applies to every project. Reduces migration surprise.
  10. #60323 refactor(client): share the persistent pty protocol — Moves the persistent PTY socket protocol out of the TUI pane into @opencode/client/solid so the Desktop terminal can reuse it (stacked with #60322/#60329).

UI-level fixes moving quickly: #60335 mobile question options/submit reachable, #60336 # in file search base, #60334 add-menu shortcuts inside bounds, #60333 Markdown frontmatter as YAML block, #60221 group added projects in settings.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Provider & transport configurability — Custom base URL/API key for any LLM (#59972), insecure HTTP for authenticated internal MCPs (#57012), per-server TLS trust (#60039). Users increasingly run OpenCode behind corporate networks and private gateways.
  • Programmable automation primitives — Code Mode schedule conditions (#60028, #60140) and exec variable substitution (#7487 — the top-voted open feature request) show demand for config-as-code without model round-trips.
  • Long-running/agentic session control — /goal in v2.2.1 formalizes objective-driven loops; schedules plus Code Mode checks extend the same idea to unattended runs.
  • Cost and quota transparency — Hidden title/summary LLM calls missing from session cost (#46371) and repeated free-tier accounting complaints.
  • Enterprise policy controls — Org-required Console sign-in (#58159) and integration connect/use policies (#60315).
  • Media efficiency — By-reference image loading (#60116) plus default image generation in v2.2.2.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Quota and rate-limit opacity — The single loudest theme: #59387 (104 comments), #60317, #60320, #60328, #59975. Symptoms include free-tier resets that never fire, paid accounts blocked on "unlimited" models, and retry countdowns that loop indefinitely.
  • Hangs with no diagnostics — Desktop sessions stuck in Working/Thinking after the Bun runtime switch (#58786) and v2.2.1 stalling for minutes on trivial prompts (#60330). No errors surfaced, which makes triage hard.
  • Local state growth and process leaks — Unbounded event table growth to 13 GB (#33356), MCP child processes accumulating until OOM (#46035), orphaned MCP descendants on disconnect (#46253).
  • Permission enforcement gaps — external_directory bypassed via shell on POSIX and PowerShell (#56288, #46398); denials losing their reason in MCP wrappers (#60102) compounded the confusion.
  • Billing and cost accounting — Real provider charges for title/summary generation that never appear in session cost (#46371).
  • Provider/model edge cases — Deterministic 400s from a Unicode × (#46378) and recursive JSON schemas rejected by some models when an MCP is enabled (#45823).
  • Compaction reliability — Manual /compact streams the full history without a context-fit check, producing upstream request failures (#46164).
  • Migration friction — V1→V2 imports needed an explicit acknowledgment (#60084); multiple "no way to add a custom URL/API key anymore" reports (#59972) suggest the provider setup path regressed in v2.

Note: no Discussion data was provided, so the Hot Discussions section is omitted.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-10-30

Source: github.com/earendil-works/pi
Window: Last 24 hours (data through 2026-10-29)

Today's Highlights

No new Pi releases were published in the last 24 hours. Activity was dominated by provider compatibility and prompt-cache correctness: OpenRouter context-limit 400s (#10497) are the most-commented issue, while dynamic tool ordering/system-prompt changes (#10024, #11529) and OpenAI-specific fields sent to compatible providers (#9508) continue to create cost and error-handling problems. Long-session stability also surfaced strongly, with a V8 OOM crash report (#11570) and a render-path performance regression (#11567), while the community highlighted a Rust port of Pi’s headless core (#11503).

Hot Issues

  1. #10497 — OpenRouter Error: 400 [OPEN, bug, inprogress]
    Context-length overflows on OpenRouter requests surface as raw 400 errors, especially for extensions that inject file contents into context. With 13 comments, it is the most-discussed issue in the window and points to a need for better preflight token accounting and provider-error normalization.

  2. #9656 — Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript in fullscreen on Windows + Zellij [OPEN, bug]
    A terminal-input handling inconsistency specific to Windows → Alacritty → Zellij. It has 12 comments and 5 👍, the highest reaction count among open bugs, suggesting multiplexer compatibility is a meaningful UX pain point.

  3. #9508 — pi-ai sends unsupported OpenAI-specific request fields/roles/auth to compatible providers [OPEN, bug]
    Third-party OpenAI-compatible providers reject Pi requests with 400/422 because OpenAI-specific fields, roles, or auth headers leak through. Nine comments since September indicate a persistent interoperability gap rather than a one-off provider issue.

  4. #10024 — Mid-run tool set change moves the head of the system prompt and re-bills the conversation [OPEN]
    Dynamic tool selection re-derives the rendered tool bullet list from the live set, changing the system prompt during a run and invalidating prompt caching. Five comments and 2 👍 reflect cost-sensitive user concern.

  5. #11157 — Extensions that sendMessage at session_start turn every session into a legacy transcript [OPEN, inprogress, prio:p0]
    Extensions that inject a message before Pi’s system message break transcript assumptions, including Anthropic’s system field behavior. The p0 label and three comments signal a core/extension ordering contract that needs to be made explicit.

  6. #11570 — V8 OOM (SIGABRT) in long sessions [CLOSED, no-action]
    Long-running sessions (~8 MB session files, 2+ days) crash with FatalProcessOutOfMemory from giant ConsString flattening/regex replacement inside flatMap. With five production crash reports, this is a high-severity stability signal despite being closed as no-action.

  7. #11527 — Bedrock: a new BedrockRuntimeClient is created for every request [OPEN]
    Each model call creates a fresh client, credential provider, and HTTP/2 session. With SSO profiles this can trigger a GetRoleCredentials round trip per request, adding latency and credential churn.

  8. #11529 — Tool order depends on registration order, so the same tools can bust the prompt cache [OPEN]
    getCurrentTools() returns insertion order, so tools that reconnect or load via tool_search move to the end of the map. This breaks prompt-cache stability and connects directly to the cost issues in #10024.

  9. #11567 — Typing slows down in long sessions: getSessionName() scans every entry on each render [CLOSED, bug, no-action]
    At ~400k entries, key-to-render p50 rises from 1.5 ms to 21 ms, with 94% of busy CPU in SessionManager.getSessionName(). The issue was closed no-action, but the profile is concrete and likely to recur.

  10. #11538 — google-generative-ai: streamed parts with separate thought signatures are merged or dropped [OPEN]
    The Google stream parser coalesces text/thinking parts and retains only the last thoughtSignature, losing replay fidelity for thinking continuity. Two comments, but provider-side correctness issues tend to affect multiple models.

Key PR Progress

  1. #11545 — Anthropic message threads [OPEN]
    Adds support for Anthropic’s server-side message threads: when a session ID is set and caching is on, Pi can send only new messages instead of the full history each turn. This could materially reduce token usage and cost.

  2. #11562 — Start new sessions in the cwd’s default directory [OPEN]
    Fixes session storage semantics when a session is opened with a cwd from another project. /new, /fork, and /clone now use the session’s cwd default folder instead of treating the old folder as a custom --session-dir.

  3. #11546 — Cap pi.exec output at 256 MiB [CLOSED]
    Bounds combined stdout/stderr via ExecOptions.maxBuffer, terminates oversized commands, and returns truncated/killed status. A practical safeguard against runaway memory use in agent-executed commands.

  4. #11577 — Pick the smaller of PNG and JPEG when resizing images [CLOSED]
    Fixes the resize path always preferring PNG when it fit under the byte limit, even when the JPEG was much smaller. Directly addresses #11550 and avoids unnecessary payload inflation.

  5. #11572 — Do not retry Zhipu usage-limit errors (code 1308) [CLOSED]
    Zhipu/Z.ai plan caps return HTTP 429 with code 1308; the generic 429 pattern previously made Pi retry futilely. The fix distinguishes a quota cap from transient rate limiting.

  6. #11565 — Stop writing OSC 133 prompt markers in regular mode [CLOSED]
    Prevents TUI messages from being interpreted as shell prompts by terminals that display OSC 7501 program status, such as Rex and newer iTerm2. Fixes disappearing “working” indicators.

  7. #11556 — Let the SDK stream resolve auth for summaries [CLOSED]
    Fixes compaction, branch summaries, and bug-report summaries in createAgentSession sessions by letting modelRuntime.streamSimple resolve stored OAuth credentials instead of passing an access token as apiKey.

  8. #11544 — Kill the daemon’s commands when it is terminated [CLOSED]
    Prevents orphaned commands when a local Unix daemon is closed: the daemon now handles SIGTERM so kill_all runs instead of dying before cleanup.

  9. #11543 — Strip private-parameter CSI sequences in stripAnsi [CLOSED]
    Fixes ANSI stripping for sequences with private prefix bytes (<, =, >), so SGR mouse reports and secondary device attributes no longer leak fragments like 35;59;1M into rendered text.

  10. #11571 — Warn when an npm package update leaves the installed version unchanged [CLOSED]
    Addresses a registry-cache mismatch between npm view and npm install <name>@latest during pi update --extensions, making a silent no-op update visible to the user.

Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11503 — pi-rs: a Rust port of the headless core
    A community Rust port of Pi 0.74.2’s headless core (agent loop, seven built-in tools, session JSONL, CLI surface, system prompt), with behavioral parity verified “atom by atom.” The author also shares a DeepSeek API compatibility finding. One comment and 1 👍.

Q&A

  • #11574 — How to upload an npmjs package to Pi package source?
    A package author asks how to publish and share a Pi package with the community. The lack of an obvious answer highlights a documentation/discovery gap around third-party package distribution.

Feature Request Trends

  • Provider abstraction hardening: sanitize OpenAI-specific fields for compatible providers (#9508), preserve Google thought signatures (#11538), reuse Bedrock clients (#11527), and handle provider-specific auth metadata correctly.
  • Prompt-cache stability and cost accounting: stable system-prompt heads and tool ordering (#10024, #11529), Bedrock cache warming (#11528), OpenRouter session IDs (#10022), and authoritative OpenRouter cost/BYOK data (#8940).
  • Long-session reliability: OOM crashes (#11570), render-time scans (#11567), context-usage accounting (#11534), and token-estimation clamping (#10988).
  • MCP and tool discovery: namespace-scoped tool_search queries (#11558), robust WWW-Authenticate parsing (#11539), and deterministic tool ordering for cache stability.
  • Extension contracts and packaging: explicit session_start message-ordering rules (#11157), recoverable unsupported image formats (#11552), configurable OAuth/Copilot timeouts (#11549), and clearer package publishing guidance (#11574).
  • Terminal UX portability: Windows/Zellij wheel handling (#9656), Apple Terminal Shift+Enter behavior (#11559), RTL rendering (#11580), and cleaner OSC/CSI handling (#11565, #11543).

Developer Pain Points

  • Provider-specific 400/422 failures remain a recurring tax. OpenAI-compatible endpoints, OpenRouter context limits, Google thought signatures, Bedrock credentials, and Zhipu quota errors all require provider-aware handling rather than generic request paths.
  • Prompt-cache invalidation is costly and hard to see. Dynamic tool selection, registration-order changes, and system-prompt head movement can silently re-bill conversations; users are asking for deterministic ordering and better cost visibility.
  • Long sessions degrade or crash. Large session files trigger V8 OOMs, per-render scans, and context-accounting problems, making multi-day agent sessions risky.
  • Extensions can violate core assumptions. Injecting messages at session_start, using tools.-prefixed names with small local models, or emitting unsupported image formats can break transcripts or provider requests.
  • Terminal and multiplexer differences create inconsistent UX. Windows/Zellij, Apple Terminal, RTL text, and OSC/CSI sequences all produce platform-specific behavior that is difficult for users to diagnose.
  • Session storage and resumption semantics are confusing. Opening a session from another project can change where /new, /fork, and /clone save, and --session-dir detection has been mistaken for custom storage.
  • Community package distribution lacks a clear path. The npm package publishing question and the Gondolin packaging fix (#11582) both point to onboarding/documentation friction for extension authors.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-30

Source: github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code · Data window: updates through 2026-10-29

1. Today's Highlights

The CLI shipped v0.26.4, a light release whose only user-facing feature is host-theme inheritance for generated UI views; the matching TypeScript SDK v0.1.26 and Desktop v0.26.4 were published alongside it. Engineering velocity is concentrated almost entirely in CI and release reliability: of the 20 most-commented PRs, more than half are infrastructure hardening (macOS suite partitioning, Web Shell smoke isolation, runner routing, Maven cache correctness, release notifier reconciliation). The most substantive open discussion remains context immutability for self-hosted models (#14215), where low prompt-processing speed makes mutable context expensive.

2. Releases

Release Notes
v0.26.4 (release) Primary CLI release. No known breaking changes. Feature: feat(generated-ui): follow the host theme in generated views (#15798). Release body is a placeholder (_See the complete change list below._), so the changelog is effectively the PR list.
sdk-typescript-v0.1.26 Bundles CLI 0.26.4, built from the same branch/ref as the SDK. The release body still contains stale text referencing CLI 0.26.3, suggesting a template/automation artifact worth cleaning up.
desktop-v0.26.4 Includes fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped (#15794) by @yiliang114, plus managed-session documentation updates.
v0.26.3-nightly.20261028.ca204559a7 Nightly cut from release/v0.26.3-nightly.20261028.ca204559a7; carries the same fix(config) change and managed docs edits.

Takeaway: a coordinated CLI + SDK + Desktop release train at 0.26.4. The only net-new product capability is theme inheritance for generated views; everything else is carried forward from 0.26.3.

3. Hot Issues

Only 3 issues were updated in the 24h window, so all three are covered rather than a top-10 selection.

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified · OPEN · type/bug, autofix/skip · 84 comments A bot-filed main-branch CI failure that has now been open for 10 days with 84 comments and no 👍. The extreme comment count on an autofix/skip-labeled item signals an automation loop or repeated human triage rather than genuine community debate — the single highest-noise item in the tracker.

  2. #14215 — Context immutability for self-hosted models · OPEN · P2, feature-request, performance, memory, caching, context-performance, need-discussion · 7 comments, 1 👍 The most substantive community request in the window. The reporter argues that features like memories, dreams, suggestions, and sessions all assume fast prompt processing; on self-hosted hardware with slow prefill, mutable context becomes prohibitively expensive. Requested behavior is an immutable context mode that preserves prefix-cache hits. Labeled need-discussion, so maintainer input is the blocker.

  3. #15251 — Fleet Shepherd Dashboard · OPEN · 0 comments Auto-maintained operational dashboard for the repo's agent fleet. Its current state is notable: the tick reports 2 autofix runs wedged in queued (oldest 2026-10-...), with syncs: 0 · dispatches: 0 · releases: 0. This is effectively a public health signal that the autofix pipeline is stalled.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15871 — refactor(managed-agent): split server into Maven modules (@doudouOUC) Decomposes the Managed Agent Server into six production Maven modules plus one unpublished verification module, with framework-neutral contracts defining boundaries between control-plane orchestration, Runtime Broker orchestration, persistence, and adapters. The largest architectural change in flight.

  2. #15870 — refactor(managed): remove persisted public message snapshots (@doudouOUC) Removes persisted public message snapshots from the managed server — a data-model simplification that likely reduces storage growth and snapshot/strea m divergence.

  3. #11854 — feat: add hybrid code mode (@DragonnZhang) Long-running (since 2026-09-14) feature adding a Codex-aligned tools.mode enum: direct, code_mode, code_mode_only. In code_mode, ordinary tools stay directly callable while also exposing an isolated exec JavaScript tool with nested JS declarations. The most significant capability addition under review.

  4. #15887 — feat(serve): enable remote access from settings without restarting (@yiliang114) Adds Settings → Connections → Allow remote connections to a running qwen serve. Remote access defaults off; a local operator can enable it live, then copy the address and a separate bearer token into another Web Shell's connection form. Meaningful UX win for daemon workflows.

  5. #15634 — feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn (@Eric-GoodBoy-Tech) Adds a fourth channel dispatchMode, inject: messages arriving mid-turn go to the running turn's mid-turn queue and are read at the next tool-batch boundary instead of being buffered until turn end. Directly addresses agent responsiveness in channel sessions.

  6. #15888 — fix(ci): partition the complete macOS test suite into bounded jobs (@yiliang114) Splits macOS CI into seven jobs (three CLI shards, two core shards, remaining workspace suites, standalone/runtime scripts) with the original check retained as an aggregate gate. Stacked on #15884/#15883. A direct response to macOS suite timeouts.

  7. #15886 + #15884 — Web Shell smoke isolation (@yiliang114) #15886 pins browser smoke to ubuntu-latest for every admitted run, decoupled from the shared Linux runner fleet; #15884 moves Chromium profiles and shared-memory temp files onto the runner temp directory. Together these target the recurring smoke failure tracked in #15060.

  8. #15885 — fix(ci): route the E2E build job through the pool-first runner expression (@yiliang114) Aligns the E2E shared build job with the repo-wide routing convention: prefer self-hosted ecs-qwen when enabled, fall back to hosted Ubuntu, plus the standard self-hosted disk setup. Closes a routing inconsistency.

  9. #15854 — perf(release): reuse verified native audio prebuilds across releases (@yiliang114) Reuses native audio prebuilds from a successful official main release when build inputs match; validated cache hits skip the entire native build matrix, with any lookup/download/validation failure falling back to rebuilding all five targets. A clear release-latency win.

  10. #15829 — fix(vscode): keep sibling model settings when writing provider config (@2SinceJuly) Fixes a real data-loss bug: configuring a Coding Plan or provider from the VS Code companion rewrote settings.model with only name, silently deleting sibling keys. Now writes name and its paired baseUrl key-by-key. High user impact relative to its small diff.

Also worth watching: #15852 (release notifiers file issues only on real failures and reconcile stale ones), #15730 (job token for publish checkout), #15274 / #15286 (Maven cache/result-preservation hardening, both autofix/needs-human), #15771 (Actions queue census on the Fleet Shepherd dashboard), #11486 (qwen update --target-version).

5. Hot Discussions

Omitted — no Discussion data was provided in this dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Context and cache economics for self-hosted deployments. #14215 is the clearest signal: prefix-cache preservation, context immutability, and lower prefill cost. The roadmap/context-performance + scope/memory + scope/caching label cluster indicates this is a recognized roadmap axis, not a one-off.
  • Tool-invocation architecture. #11854 (tools.mode: direct / code_mode / code_mode_only) points toward a Codex-aligned model where tools are callable both directly and from an isolated JS exec sandbox.
  • Live/remote serving ergonomics. #15887 seeks zero-restart remote access with token-based auth for qwen serve — the daemon is being treated as a first-class deployment target.
  • Mid-turn message injection. #15634 requests interruptible, tool-boundary-aware message delivery in channel sessions instead of end-of-turn buffering.
  • Deterministic, offline-capable installation. #11486 (--target-version without npm discovery) reflects demand for pinned, reproducible standalone installs, including custom QWEN_UPDATE_BASE_URL mirrors.
  • Editor integration fidelity. #15829 shows VS Code companion config writes must be non-destructive to sibling settings — a "don't lose my config" class of request.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. CI instability is the dominant tax. At least 8 of the top 20 PRs are CI fixes. Recurring themes: shared runner network contention (#15886), Chromium temp/shared-memory behavior in Web Shell smoke (#15884), macOS suite duration (#15888), inconsistent runner routing (#15885), and Maven cache write-back failure modes (#15274, #15286). Contributors are spending review bandwidth on test infrastructure rather than product code.
  2. Autofix automation is stalling, not helping. Issue #15251 reports 2 autofix runs wedged in queued; #14724 has accumulated 84 comments on a main-CI failure; two autofix/needs-human PRs (#15274, #15286) have sat open since 2026-10-22. The bot produces volume, but a growing share requires human rescue.
  3. Release automation false positives. #15852 documents that both fan-out release notifiers treat cancelled runs as failures and file issues, and that neither can close those issues when a later attempt ships. Combined with the placeholder v0.26.4 notes and the stale "0.26.3" text inside the 0.1.26 SDK release body, release metadata is drifting from reality.
  4. Silent config mutations destroy user state. Two independent tickets in one window — Desktop's fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped (#15794) and VS Code's settings.model overwrite (#15829) — indicate a systemic pattern: writers replace config objects rather than merging keys.
  5. Self-hosted users feel like second-class citizens. #14215 articulates the frustration directly: cutting-edge features (memories, dreams, suggestions, sessions) are designed around fast hosted prompt processing and degrade badly on slower self-hosted hardware.
  6. Opaque or missing release notes. v0.26.4's changelog ships as _See the complete change list below._, forcing users to reconstruct changes from the PR list.

Digest generated from GitHub metadata only. Issue/PR bodies were truncated in the source data; comment counts were unavailable for PRs and are reported as-is for issues.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-30

Issues: 170 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-29 18:48 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-30

数据窗口： 过去 24 小时，截至 2026-10-29。
数据说明： Issue 为按评论数排序的前 50 个；PR 为前 30 个样本。提供的数据中没有 PR 评论数，因此 PR 排名基于提供的排序和标签。

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 正处于发布与分诊的极高活跃阶段：过去 24 小时有 170 个 Issue 和 500 个 PR 得到更新，其中 131 个活跃 Issue 和 291 个开放 PR，同时还有一个补丁版本发布。新版本 v2026.10.9 是安全与依赖加固补丁，而不是功能版本。Issue 队列主要由核心可靠性主题主导——会话状态生命周期、崩溃/唤醒恢复、记忆提升、消息丢失和提供商认证——而不是外观类请求。项目正在快速交付安全修复，但多个 P0/P1 可靠性 Issue 仍未关闭且没有关联修复 PR，因此整体健康度可概括为 高速推进但可靠性风险升高。

2. 发布

v2026.10.9 — 安全/依赖补丁

发布说明重点介绍了正在修补的运行时依赖漏洞：

  • MCP schema 校验： fast-uri 4.2.3 会拒绝格式错误的 URI scheme 和 host。
  • 输入边界： 过大的 Zod 集合会在 A2UI 和 Discord 嵌入式应用 SDK 中被提前拒绝。
  • IMAP 发件人解析： 迁移到 nodemailer 10.1.4，加强伪造发件人处理。

破坏性变更： 发布说明未提及。
迁移说明： 未提及。这似乎是一个可直接替换的补丁版本。
建议： 由于该版本明确以安全为重点，建议升级。

  • 长生命周期会话： Issue #154482 请求为永久 MAIN 会话历史提供受支持的生命周期——按范围导出/裁剪或滚动——因为以连续性为重点的部署无法限制 transcript_events。相关：Issue #112638 关于 session.maintenance 未能限制存储。
  • 团队/多 Agent 组织： Issue #153686 请求在团队模式下保留每个 Agent 下的命名会话组，而不是扁平化为 pinned/recent。相关的路由隔离问题出现在 Issue #126533 和 Issue #154739。
  • 无障碍与 UI 打磨： Issue #154524 请求将聊天消息暴露为标题以便屏幕阅读器导航；Issue #167415 报告侧边栏行在悬停状态间展开/打开与一键 Archive 交换位置，存在误归档风险。
  • 技能学习 / 评估： Issue #150250 提出一种 Skill Workshop 能力，用于验证普通工作中的学习覆盖率和行为复用。

对下一版本的预测： 最强的近期信号是安全/依赖补丁、模型目录和 thinking profile 工作、记忆索引韧性，以及有针对性的状态/UI 修复。更广泛的架构请求——永久 MAIN 会话生命周期、团队模式命名组，以及深度的会话状态租约重设计——除非维护者将其优先作为发布阻断项，否则不太可能在下一个补丁中落地。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 用户依赖连续性。 长生命周期 MAIN 会话、记忆提升和记录保留是反复出现的关切。当短期召回上限或提升过滤器行为异常时，用户会失去持久个人 Agent 的核心价值（#150635、#164923、#154482）。
  • 多 Agent Gateway 是生产工作负载。 用户报告租约争用、跨会话信封、多 Agent 扇出和工作区特定的提升失败。他们需要隔离和清晰的所有权语义，而不仅仅是配置选项（#159094、#126533、#154739）。
  • 通道可靠性很重要。 Telegram、Discord、Matrix 和 Tlon 的 Issue 涵盖消息丢失、媒体未送达、提及门控、引用边界和重启后绑定丢失。这些是生产集成 Bug，而不是边缘场景功能请求（#160762、#187588、#164065、PR #177691、PR #187778）。
  • CLI 支持的提供商路径仍然脆弱。 Codex 和 claude-cli 的 Issue 涉及认证导入、OAuth 刷新锁、来源拒绝、格式错误的流式参数、重复 MCP 服务器和模型目录不匹配。用户希望重试、清晰的原因码和平台一致性（#161341、#156442、#155396、#155457、#164690）。
  • 满意信号： 安全补丁活跃，社区参与度高，维护者正在跨模型目录、记忆索引和 UI 进行合并/重构。不满意信号： 多个 P0 已开放数周，许多高价值 Issue 带有 stale 或 needs-product-decision 标签，发布验证仍会遇到 flaky 测试。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告 —— 个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态

日期： 2026-10-30
项目： OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw
数据说明： 各摘要使用的采样窗口以及评论/反应数据的可得性不同。下文的健康评分为分析师定性评分（0–10），并非直接基准测试。IronClaw 在本窗口内无活动。

1. 生态概览

个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态正处于高活跃度但高度关注可靠性的阶段。各项目已不再主要围绕功能新颖性竞争；它们正趋同于持久化多通道运行、会话状态持久化、记忆正确性、提供商/认证韧性以及运行安全。OpenClaw 按吞吐量是规模最大、最活跃的参考点，而 Hermes Agent、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 则占据更窄但技术上各具特色的细分领域。发布节奏并不均衡：只有 OpenClaw 交付了一个补丁，其他项目则在积累修复，等待后续版本切出。生态的主要风险并非贡献量，而是合并/评审能力以及尚未解决的高严重度可靠性欠账。

2. 活跃度对比

项目 Issues（近 24 小时） PRs（近 24 小时） 发布状态 健康评分
OpenClaw 170 个更新；131 个活跃/开放 500 个更新；291 个开放；209 个已合并/关闭 v2026.10.9 安全/依赖补丁；无破坏性变更 7.2/10 —— 迭代速度快、安全响应及时，但 P0/P1 可靠性风险偏高
Hermes Agent 17 个更新；17 个开放；0 个关闭 50 个更新；37 个开放；13 个已合并/关闭 无发布；发布前稳定期低迷 6.4/10 —— 吞吐量强，但发布停滞且积压增长
IronClaw 0 0 无 不适用 —— 本窗口内休眠
QwenPaw 13 个更新；9 个关闭 41 个更新；27 个开放；14 个已合并/关闭 无发布；正在稳定 2.3.0-beta.1 6.8/10 —— 活跃且响应及时，但 beta 版脆弱，且大型 PR 评审受限
ZeroClaw 1 个更新；1 个关闭；0 个活跃开放 50 个更新；49 个开放；1 个已合并/关闭 无发布；v0.9.0 前筹备中 5.5/10 —— 管线较深，但合并速度低，作者行动项积压

解读： OpenClaw 的 PR 更新量约为同类的 10×，并且是本窗口内唯一交付发布版本的项目。QwenPaw 在活跃同类中拥有最健康的合并比例，而 ZeroClaw 的评审瓶颈最为明显。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相较同类的优势

  • 规模： 24 小时内 500 个 PR 更新、209 个已合并/关闭 PR、170 个 Issue 更新 —— 远高于 Hermes、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw。
  • 发布响应能力： 在其他项目未发布任何版本时，交付了一个安全/依赖补丁。
  • 广度： 覆盖多 Agent 网关运行、会话状态生命周期、记忆提升、模型目录/思考配置、Discord/Codex 持久化、记忆索引韧性、沙箱以及多种通道适配器。
  • 社区引力： 在此集合中拥有最大的可见贡献者和 Issue 管线；很可能成为持久化 Agent 运行时的实际参考实现。

技术路线差异 OpenClaw 是以网关为中心、运行时较重的架构。其 Issue 集中在状态生命周期租约、崩溃/唤醒恢复、记忆提升、消息丢失防护以及提供商认证上——也就是持久化多 Agent 运行时最艰难的操作核心。相比之下：

  • Hermes 更偏向桌面端/消息能力对齐以及安装/更新。
  • QwenPaw 更偏向控制台/插件/PawApp。
  • ZeroClaw 更偏向系统层面，围绕事件溯源持久化、Goal Mode 和 ZeroCode TUI。
  • IronClaw 在本窗口内不活跃。

社区规模对比 OpenClaw 的活跃度比同类高一个数量级：PR 更新为 500，而 Hermes/QwenPaw/ZeroClaw 为 41–50；Issue 更新为 170，而后者为 1–17。然而，OpenClaw 也集中了最多未解决的 P0/P1 可靠性 Issue，因此规模并不等同于全面更优的健康度。

安全/沙箱/密钥 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 工作区作用域、密钥脱敏、审批路由、提示注入误报、CLI 密钥掩码、Code Mode 安全

Agent 循环与成本控制 QwenPaw、ZeroClaw、Hermes、OpenClaw 死循环防护、可配置循环中断、成本覆盖、负定价、计费正确性、用量可见性

共同信号： 用户正把这些系统当作生产基础设施，而不是演示项目。最高价值的工作越来越集中在可预测的状态、可观测的失败和安全自动化上，而非新的 UI 界面。

5. 差异化分析

项目 功能重点 目标用户 架构信号
OpenClaw 持久化多通道、多 Agent 运行时；会话生命周期；记忆提升；模型目录；沙箱 高级用户、运维人员、多通道 Agent 部署 以网关为中心的运行时，具备状态租约、记忆管线、通道适配器、安全边界
Hermes Agent 桌面端/消息能力对齐、安装/更新可靠性、Slack/Telegram/Discord 命令、技能目录 桌面端与无头/远程用户；多配置网关运维人员；Slack 团队 桌面客户端 + 网关 + 包/安装管理器 + 技能/插件
QwenPaw 插件生态、Web 控制台、PawApp SDK/控制平面、JEV 安全模式、Auto-Dream 记忆 开发者、控制台/中枢管理员、beta 测试者、插件作者 插件隔离架构、Console/PawApp 分层、记忆召回管线、提供商集成
ZeroClaw 持久化事件溯源会话、Goal Mode、ZeroCode TUI、成本控制、通道丰富度 需要持久性、可审计性、TUI 工作流的运维人员和开发者 面向系统的运行时，具备仅追加会话历史、目标生命周期、MCP/服务健壮性
IronClaw 本窗口内无活动 未知 无法评估

关键差异： OpenClaw 最广、最“平台化”；Hermes 最偏桌面端/安装运维；QwenPaw 最偏插件/控制台；ZeroClaw 最偏持久性/事件历史。OpenClaw 以广度和规模竞争，而不是单一狭窄工作流。

6. 社区动能与成熟度

第一梯队 —— 规模领先者，快速迭代 + 持续交付

  • OpenClaw： 活跃度极高，贡献者基础庞大，已交付安全补丁。按规模看成熟度高，但由于未解决的 P0/P1 会话状态与恢复故障，可靠性风险也最高。

第二梯队 —— 快速迭代者，正在稳定

  • Hermes Agent： PR 吞吐量和贡献者多样性较强，但 Issue 关闭数为零且无发布。积压压力以及安装/更新回归是主要拖累。
  • QwenPaw： 合并速度快，分诊响应及时，但存在 2.3.0-beta.1 回归和大型 PR 评审瓶颈。首次贡献者信号良好。
  • ZeroClaw： 管线深、路线图阶段划分清晰，但 1 个合并对 49 个开放 PR。评审吞吐量和作者跟进是瓶颈；处于 v0.9.0 前。

第三梯队 —— 休眠

  • IronClaw： 报告窗口内无活动。

动能解读： OpenClaw 正以生态领先的规模迭代并交付。QwenPaw 相对其体量迭代最快。Hermes 在积累修复但未发布。ZeroClaw 有架构雄心，但受合并能力制约。

7. 趋势信号

  1. 持久、可回放的状态正在成为基本要求。
    OpenClaw 的会话状态故障、ZeroClaw 的仅追加事件历史、Hermes 的迁移/会话恢复缺陷，以及 QwenPaw 的回退/决策持久化需求，都指向同一项要求：Agent 必须能在崩溃、重启、迁移和压缩后继续存活，且不丢失工作。

  2. 记忆是信任面，而不是功能勾选项。
    静默记忆丢失、提升不一致、召回泄漏和并发写入数据丢失在 OpenClaw、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 中均有出现。开发者应把记忆视为事务性、可观测的子系统，并具备明确的成功/失败语义。

  3. 静默失败比显性失败更糟。
    Hermes 的 Slack 状态回归、QwenPaw 的“success=True”记忆丢失，以及 ZeroClaw 的 600s 静默等待，都表明用户对 bug 的容忍度高于不可见 bug。原因码、警告和遥测现在已成为产品需求。

  4. 多通道一致性是竞争基线。
    Telegram、Slack、Discord、Matrix 和 Web 控制台都需要一致的媒体处理、富消息、输入中/状态指示器，以及重启后持久的绑定。通道特定回归是生产阻塞项。

  5. 提供商抽象仍然脆弱。
    Codex/claude-cli 认证、OAuth 锁、OpenRouter 定价/密钥轮换、思考控制、本地模型发现和模型目录不匹配反复出现。稳健的提供商层需要重试、认证恢复、成本正确性和清晰诊断。

  6. 安全控制必须精准，而不是表演式。
    沙箱路径逃逸、密钥暴露、审批路由和提示注入误报在所有活跃项目中都有出现。过度拦截普通文本会带来满意度风险；拦截不足则是安全风险。开发者需要经过校准、决策可解释的护栏。

  7. 安装/更新/打包是 Agent 产品的一部分。
    PM 修复失败、部分克隆、PyInstaller 资源遗漏、插件加载失败，以及更新回执卡在“running”都不是次要问题——它们决定用户能否可靠地运行 Agent。

  8. 评审/设计能力是生态瓶颈。
    ZeroClaw 单日 49 个开放/1 个关闭 PR，以及 QwenPaw 的 XXXL PR 队列表明，贡献量可能超过维护者带宽。拥有清晰架构决策记录和更小可评审 PR 的项目，将更快把社区动能转化为已交付的可靠性。

对 AI agent 开发者的结论： 应围绕持久状态、可观测记忆、通道一致性、提供商韧性、精准安全以及可靠的安装/更新路径来构建。功能广度很重要，但在本窗口内，生态的稀缺资源是在持久化、多通道运行下的可信度。

Hermes Agent — 项目摘要

Hermes Agent 正处于高吞吐的维护阶段：过去 24 小时内有 50 个 PR 被触及（37 个开放，13 个已合并/关闭），同期有 17 条 Issue 更新——且全部仍处于开放状态。未切发布，因此已合并的工作正在累积，等待下一个版本，而不是已经交付。Issue 流入明显偏向新报告：17 条中有 6 条创建于 2026-10-29，其中若干引用了 v0.22.5 和当前 main，这表明近期构建上存在活跃的内部试用。活动量高，但信号几乎完全是 bug 修复与加固工作——没有新功能随版本落地，且开放 Issue 积压的增长速度快于关闭速度（今日关闭 0 条）。整体健康度表现为稳定但承压于积压，回归明显集中在 Slack 集成、安装/更新路径和 Desktop 会话状态附近。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度与影响范围排序：

P1 — 安装阻塞项

  • #135910 · pm repair 无法在大小写不敏感文件系统上提交依赖环境。shutil.copytree 在捆绑的 CPython terminfo 上因 Errno 17 失败；随后所有经 PM 路由的操作都会失败。标记 sweeper:risk-compatibility、os/macos。未见修复 PR。

P2 — 崩溃与数据访问回归

  • #146537 · TUI 会话切换器（Ctrl+X / /sessions）会通过 shortModel 中的 Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replace') 杀死整个 TUI，触发条件是某个活动会话行的 model 为 NULL。硬崩溃，提交于 2026-10-29。未见修复 PR。
  • #143150 · Desktop 在 gateway.multiplex_profiles: true 迁移后无法恢复先前会话 → storage_unavailable。阻塞对历史聊天数据的访问。未见修复 PR。
  • #110374 / #112866 / #132594 · Slack 状态/输入指示器在 slack-sdk ≥ 3.44 上静默失效。功能上只是表面问题，但会影响每一轮 Slack 交互。相关开放 PR #145832 修复的是 Slack display_name 处理，并非此回归。
  • #137098 · 对于 OpenRouter 的路由/可变价格 slug，成本估算会变成负数（负价格哨兵值被按面值计价）。这会侵蚀计费信任。相邻 PR #55855 处理的是上游 429 时的 OpenRouter 密钥轮换，而非定价。
  • #146502 · auxiliary.compression.model 被忽略——summary_model_override 硬编码为 None，因此压缩始终使用主模型，并在该模型变慢时卡住。
  • #146584 · Windows Desktop 启动时运行 hermes gateway ensure 两次；这次冗余的 2.5 秒调用在 5.0 秒启动中占主导。

P3 — 正确性与防护行为

  • #146586 · 当循环前已有 ≥5 个不同行时，is_runaway_repetition() 无法截断不含换行的循环——已有修复 PR：#146587。
  • #146582 · execute_code 生命周期防护会对仅仅提及 gateway 重启的文档产生误报——而且很容易被拼接绕过。既存在过度拦截，也存在拦截不足。
  • #146577 / #146578 · 更新成功后，更新回执卡在 outcome: "running"（下一次运行会将其视为中断）；部分克隆安装中 git merge-base 10 秒超时。两者均属 area/install-update，且由同一报告者提交。
  • #146495 · Linux Desktop：新建项目在 Projects 过滤器中默认未勾选。

安全标记项

  • #146564 · Kanban worker 必须将受保护写入的审批转交给已认证的 owner 响应方；worker 会话对常规审批界面不可见，因此 AGENTS.md 一类写入可能卡住，或在 owner 不可见的情况下继续执行。

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点，以用户自己的表述：

  • “Windows 上的仅前端安装” — 用户已经手动解决了分布式 agent 问题，希望 Desktop 不再假设自己与 agent 同机部署。这是工作流请求，不是 bug。
  • “静默损坏” / “静默消失” / “静默失败” — “静默”一词出现在全部三份 Slack 报告中。用户对故障的容忍度远高于对没有错误暴露面的故障；具体抱怨是协议失败只写入 debug 日志。
  • “任何依赖环境都无法提交” — 在受影响的文件系统上，P1 的 PM 故障被描述为绝对失败，而非间歇性失败。
  • “更新成功后，更新回执仍停留在 'running'” — 信任问题：日志说成功，状态却说中断。用户无法判断自己的安装是否可靠。

满意信号： 重复贡献者参与度高（Jpalmer95 提交了多个 PR，thisisnotajokee 在一天内提交了三份精确的安装-更新报告，附带版本哈希与耗时），且 bug 报告详细、可复现——这表明用户群体投入度高、技术能力强，而不是充满挫败感。

不满意信号： Slack 回归已持续至少三个版本（v0.21.5 → v0.21.6 → v0.22.5 时代），并产生了重复报告而非解决方案。#38519 请求自六月起开放，有 31 个赞，却无可见决策。两者都在累积善意负债。

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-30

1. 今日概览

QwenPaw 展现出高频维护活动：过去 24 小时内更新了 13 个 issue 和 41 个 PR，其中 9 个 issue 关闭、14 个 PR 合并/关闭，仍有 27 个处于开启状态。本周期无新版本发布，但活动高度集中在稳定 2.3.0-beta.1 分支上，该版本产生了多份回归报告（插件加载、桌面打包、可选依赖内存占用）。项目还关闭了一个长期悬而未决的 wontfix 决策——关于 agent 死循环（#6116），并落地了安全/CLI 加固（#8492、#8501）。整体健康状况为活跃但 beta 脆弱：贡献者吞吐量强劲、问题分诊响应及时，但待审的大型（XL–XXXL）PR 队列持续增长。首次贡献者（#8291、#8400）的出现表明新人上手通道健康。

2. 版本发布

本周期无。

3. 项目进展

可见窗口内有五个 PR 进入关闭/合并状态，涵盖安全、provider、控制台 UX 和网站基础设施：

  • #8492 fix(security): prevent false-positive approvals for Code Mode in JEV mode — 收紧工具审查门控，避免 Code Mode 操作被错误地自动批准；与 agent 安全直接相关。
  • #8497 fix(plugins): tolerate import cache refresh failures during plugin loading — 针对 2.3.0-beta.1 启动失败（#8473）的修复；恢复插件入口点加载。
  • #8358 fix(providers): honor thinking defaults and declared wire controls — 解决了 Console/后端不一致的问题：thinking_enabled=off 未被传递给 OpenAI 兼容 provider。
  • #5490 feat(console): navigable fullscreen image gallery for chat media — 长期功能（6 月开启）终于关闭；将工具卡片图片包裹在单个 Image.PreviewGroup 中以支持画廊导航。
  • #8253 feat(website): add JSON-driven evaluation index — 双语评估排行榜，含 Pareto 前沿和 SDK 历史。

其他推进中的工作：记忆召回加固（#8457、#7835）、CLI 密钥掩码（#8501）以及 Ollama 模型发现（#8309）。

4. 社区热点

条目 活动 链接
#6116 死循环：agent 在单轮中重复相同工具调用 9 条评论，关闭 wontfix Issue
#8464 手动 /compact 忽略会话级模型切换 4 条评论，已关闭 Issue
#8500 Auto-Dream 静默丢弃记忆，仍照常 checkpoint 2 条评论，开启 Issue
#8473 2.3.0-beta.1 中所有后端插件加载失败 2 条评论，已关闭（修复：#8497） Issue

底层需求分析：

  • Agent 循环控制是情绪最激烈的话题（9 条评论）。用户记录了系统介入前约 6 次重复的相同工具调用，浪费 token 和 API 预算。wontfix 的处置值得注意——它很可能表明一种设计立场（例如 6 次重复保护被视为“按预期工作”），而非敷衍了事。这可能会以“可配置/更早的循环中断”请求的形式再次出现。
  • 会话状态一致性（#8464）：用户在会话中途切换模型后，期望所有操作——包括 compaction——都遵循当前活动模型。根因是 active_model 解析读取的是 agent 级配置而非会话上下文。
  • 静默数据丢失（#8500）是信任风险最高的开放议题：success=True 的报告掩盖了记忆丢弃，正是这类 bug 会侵蚀用户对自主记忆功能的信心。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度排序（均为 2026-10-29 报告/更新）：

  1. 严重 — #8473 2.3.0-beta.1：所有后端插件在启动时加载失败（报告者主机上 12/12 插件）。根因：module_isolation.py:220 中未加保护的 importlib.invalidate_caches()，与此前 #8265 根因相同，为新调用点。已有修复： #8497（已关闭）。
  2. 高 — #8488 桌面/PyInstaller 构建遗漏 visual_compression 资源 → FileNotFoundError: atlas-gray-native.ts；Visual Compact 静默失效，无用户可见警告。2.3.0-beta.1 打包回归。开启，无关联修复 PR。
  3. 高 — #8500 Auto-Dream 在提取步骤无法解析 agent 回复时静默丢弃整天的记忆，却仍然 checkpoint 文件导致永不重试。报告 success=True 且无遥测。开启，无关联修复 PR。
  4. 中 — #8464 手动 /compact 总是使用 agent 级 active_model，当该模型严格校验 compaction 参数时返回 400 失败。已关闭。
  5. 中 — #8490 打开语音转录设置仅仅为了检查可用性，就把 whisper 导入服务器进程（约 690 MB RSS，永不释放）。开启。
  6. 低 — #8486 工具调用 <> 图标左边缘被裁切——容器缺少水平内边距。外观问题。开启。

回归簇： 四个开放 bug 中有三个（#8488、#8490、#8486）来自 2.3.0-beta.1 时期的构建，表明该 beta 在 GA 前需要一次集中的稳定化冲刺。一个安全相关的加固 PR，#8501（在 env list/env set 中掩码环境变量值），也解决了 CLI 中的明文密钥暴露问题。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

今日关闭的增强类 issue 涵盖 agent 控制和长会话 UX 面：

  • #6189 save_decision() API — 结构化决策持久化，以在上下文压缩后存活。强烈的框架级诉求（先有鸡还是先有蛋问题：agent 忘记决策然后无法归档它们）。
  • #4356 更细粒度的文件/工具守卫 — 只读路径、项目目录白名单，而非仅黑名单。
  • #4129 /rewind — 回滚文件/上下文以尝试替代提示或撤销 agent 造成的破坏（直接对标 Claude Code 的请求）。
  • #7740 Hub 模式管理员密码重置。
  • #8459 Web Console 中更便捷地访问未读推送消息。

对下个版本的预测： 鉴于 beta 回归负载，下一个即时版本很可能是 2.3.0-beta.2/GA 稳定化，而非功能交付。save_decision 式上下文持久性和 rewind 可能在 2.3.x 或 2.4 落地的信号：两者都针对与开放 bug #8500 相同的压缩丢失痛点类别，且项目已在投资相关记忆管道（#8457、#7835）。文件守卫粒度（#4356）与 #8492 中的 JEV/工具审查安全工作天然配对。

7. 用户反馈摘要

今日表达的痛点：

  • 成本/效率： 死循环（#6116）浪费的 token 和 API 调用——用户希望更早或可配置的循环中断。
  • 可预测性： 会话中途切换模型不被 /compact 遵循（#8464），打破了“你选什么就跑什么”的基本心智模型。
  • 对自主性的信任： 静默记忆丢失（#8500）和静默失效（#8488）比 loudly failure 更糟——用户反复要求可见的状态/警告。
  • 资源卫生： 仅仅访问设置页面就产生 690 MB RSS（#8490），在桌面/笔记本部署上很重要。
  • 运维基础： Hub 管理员仍无法重置用户密码（#7740）；密钥在 env list 中明文打印（已由 #8501 解决）。

满意度信号： 高质量、可复现的 bug 报告（尤其是来自 feng183043996，提交了 #6116、#6189、#8500 并撰写了 #8501）以及首次贡献者（#8291、#8400）表明社区参与度高。不满是beta 质量的摩擦，而非根本方向问题——若干抱怨是打包/生命周期回归而非架构性反对。

7. 用户反馈摘要

该数据集中没有直接的用户评论（评论数不可用；唯一 issue 有 1 条评论）。痛点只能从 PR/问题陈述中推断，而这些陈述异常明确：

  • 对持久化状态的信任是主导主题。用户遇到的是静默失败：并发下记忆写入丢失（#12004）、重命名后 CLI“无法恢复”（#11301）、每次启动都会忘记已打开会话的侧边栏（#11727）。
  • 静默等待是反复出现的不满点：已清除的引导请求会导致 600 秒挂起且无 UI 反馈（#11624）；没有转录时间戳就无法判断事件顺序或持续时间（#11622）。
  • 误报的安全控制降低日常使用体验——普通文本和工具输出因注入被拦截（#12068）。这是满意度风险：误触发的安全功能被报告为阻碍，而非保护。
  • 文档漂移是真实抱怨：v0.8.7 发布的翻译目录包含不正确信息，只有通过完整人工通读才发现（#12076）。这表明 i18n 发布流程缺少验证关卡。
  • 平台广度摩擦： Android 用户被完全阻断在 shell 工具之外（#12080 → #12080）。
  • 满意度信号： 无可量化信号（所有 👍 = 0）。没有证据表明用户对方向不满；有证据表明用户对可靠性边界情况不满。

存在停滞风险、需要维护者关注的条目：

存续时间（截至 2026-10-30） 条目 阻塞因素
29 天 #11301 — 持久化已提交重命名恢复 priority:p1 + needs-author-action + risk:high；价值最高但未推进的修复。
28 天 #11457 — 非取消式会话刷新 distinguished contributor，小型行为修复，没有可见评审者。
27 天 #11505 — 设置操作 + 键位绑定过滤器 needs-author-action
23 天 #11589 — 运维成本限制覆盖 有文档但未实现的配置；中等用户价值，XL 范围。
9 天 #11921 — 仅追加的会话事件历史 risk:high + size:XL；需要架构决策，而不仅仅是评审。
7 天 #12004 — 记忆仅追加 priority:p1、needs-maintainer-review；廉价修复，P1 影响。

给维护者的流程观察：

  1. 合并吞吐量是瓶颈。 49 个开放对 1 个关闭，且 45% 为 needs-author-action，这表明分诊惯例把 PR 停在作者身上，却没有清晰的重新进入路径。
  2. 两个 docs(runtime) 例外请求 PR——#12063（agent 自有状态退役，引用 #9745/#9647）和 #12037（外部记忆重排）——表明贡献者在寻求架构许可，而不是代码评审。这些是只有维护者才能解除阻塞的治理决策。
  3. ZeroCode 上的单一作者集中度（8/20 个 PR）是 bus-factor 风险；其中四个带有 needs-author-action，如果该贡献者带宽受限，问题可能加剧。
  4. 快速修复现已可用： #12068、#12080、#12061 为 size:XS/S——一次评审即可清理三个稳定性条目，并把合并速度从谷底拉起来。
